submissions.findingTextShort: A small acute crossover RCT of standardized American-ginseng extract reported selected working-memory and calmness signals, with no glucose effect.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial in 32 healthy young adults evaluated standardized Panax quinquefolius extract Cereboost, specified at 10.65% ginsenosides, across 100, 200, and 400 mg acute doses. Selected working-memory and calmness outcomes favored some doses, while blood glucose was not improved. The branded extract, acute design, outcome selectivity, dose dependence, and healthy-young-adult population are part of the proposition and must not become a generic American-ginseng cognition claim.
submissions.populationContext: Thirty-two healthy young adults in an acute randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial.
submissions.usageContext: Standardized Panax quinquefolius extract Cereboost, 10.65% ginsenosides, 100/200/400 mg acute doses.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small sample, acute exposure, branded extract and selected outcomes limit generalization. Preserve the null glucose result alongside favorable cognitive/mood signals.

submissions.findingTextShort: An 8-week crossover trial in type-2 diabetes used 3 g/day American-ginseng extract as an adjunct and reported selected glycemic/cardiovascular-marker signals.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A double-blind crossover trial in 24 people with type-2 diabetes evaluated 3 g/day American-ginseng extract added to conventional treatment for eight weeks and reported signals in HbA1c, fasting glucose and selected cardiovascular markers. This is adjunct disease-population evidence rather than evidence for metabolic wellness in healthy users, and the extract identity, concomitant treatment, small sample and short duration must remain explicit.
submissions.populationContext: Twenty-four adults with type-2 diabetes receiving conventional treatment.
submissions.usageContext: American-ginseng extract, 3 g/day for eight weeks, adjunct to conventional diabetes treatment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Do not transfer adjunct T2DM biomarker findings into general prevention, weight-management or healthy-user efficacy claims.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 review confirms a human neurocognitive evidence base for Panax quinquefolius but emphasizes formulation and population heterogeneity.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 review of American ginseng and human neurocognitive function includes double-blind randomized clinical evidence and establishes that Panax quinquefolius has a human evidence base beyond the profile's current metabolic framing. The review does not erase heterogeneity in branded extracts, doses, acute versus repeated exposure, populations, or endpoints. Asian Panax ginseng evidence must remain separate from Panax quinquefolius evidence.
submissions.usageContext: Review-level evidence for Panax quinquefolius neurocognitive studies; heterogeneous preparations and populations.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Treat as domain-expansion and evidence-mapping support, not automatic evidence-tier inflation or permission to merge Asian-ginseng studies.
